identity.title: ALMA Polarimetry of Sgr A*: Probing the Accretion Flow from the Event Horizon to the Bondi Radius

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present here multi-epoch ALMA Band 6 (230 GHz) polarimetry of Sgr A*.

evidence.quote: 1 R_S \approx 10 \mu as$ for a distance of 8.1 kpc

question.value: What are the linear and circular polarization and Faraday rotation measure of Sgr A* at 1.3 mm, and how do they vary in time, as a probe of the accretion flow?

evidence.quote: Millimeter polarimetry of Sgr A* probes the linearly polarized emission region on a scale of ~10 Schwarzschild radii
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00764.S
ALMA observed Sgr A* in Band 6 (1.3 mm wavelength) in full polarimetric continuum mode on three epochs

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs, 2 GHz each, 64 channels; centers 223.96, 225.96, 239.96, 241.96 GHz

evidence.quote: The SPW center frequencies are 223.96 GHz, 225.96 GHz, 239.96 GHz, and 241.96 GHz.
naturally-weighted synthesized beam sizes $\sim 1$ arcsec

time_on_source.value: ~3 h in epochs 1 and 2; ~5 h over 7 h in epoch 3

evidence.quote: Approximately three hours of observations were obtained in epochs 1 and 2.

what.value: Historical RM measurements of Sgr A* (BIMA+JCMT, SMA) used in structure function

evidence.quote: Historical Measurements of Rotation Measure

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA pipelines with standard a priori and calculated calibrations

evidence.quote: Data reduction was performed in CASA using pipelines that applied standard *a priori* and calculated calibrations.
Absolute flux calibration was set by observations of the moon Titan in epochs 1 and 2.
estimated flux density of 2.4 Jy, constant across all SPWs, with an accuracy of $\sim 20\%$
We rejected all baselines shorter than $50 k\lambda$ in order to eliminate any extended structure around Sgr A*.
naturally-weighted synthesized beam sizes $\sim 1$ arcsec

unstated_but_needed: Polarization calibration procedure details (leakage, D-terms, angle)
Time-binning and fitting weighting for RM fits

method.value: Image-domain point-source fits per SPW and per time slice; position fixed from Stokes I for Q,U,V

evidence.quote: Fits in the Stokes Q, U, and V domains were obtained with the point-source position fixed at the fitted peak of the Stokes I image.
We rejected all baselines shorter than $50 k\lambda$
These image-domain results are consistent with point-source fits obtained in the visibility domain.

method.value: Fit chi = chi_0 + RM lambda^2 to position angle per epoch and per time slice

evidence.quote: $\chi = \chi_0 + RM \lambda^2,$

validation.value: Calibrators observed in same way to set systematic limits

evidence.quote: We use calibrator results in this Section to set limits on systematic errors on LP fraction, CP fraction, and rotation measure.

method.value: SF^2(tau)=<(RM(t+tau)-RM(t))^2> within epochs and over epoch-averaged plus archival RMs

evidence.quote: We analyze variability in the RM using the structure function
Data reduction was performed in CASA using pipelines

used_for.value: Listed in software section; use not stated

evidence.quote: CASA, MATLAB
We find a mean CP of $\approx -1.1 \pm 0.2$%.
the change $\delta {\rm RM} = 4.93 \times 10^5 {\rm\ rad\ m^{-2}}$ across the three epochs is detected at a $5 \sigma$ threshold

findings_qualitative.value: No characteristic RM variability timescale between hours and decades; RM anticorrelated with polarized flux

evidence.quote: we do not identify any characteristic time scale between hours and decades for variability of the RM

claims.hypothesis: Mean RM of Sgr A* remains consistent with historical values
claims.finding: Consistent with RIAF accretion flow, Mdot~1e-8 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: The results confirm a mean rotation measure, ${\rm RM} \approx -5 \times 10^5 {\rm\ rad\ m^{-2}}$

claims.experiment: Compare epochs and intra-epoch fits against calibrator systematics

evidence.quote: Variability is observed for the first time in the RM on time scales that range from hours to months.
the handedness remains unchanged from that observed in past centimeter- and millimeter-wavelength detections

limitations_admitted.value: Largest fitted RMs are suspect due to phase wrap, poor fits and calibration errors at low polarization

evidence.quote: The largest fitted values of the RM are suspect for three reasons
